title: Highest New Home Sales in Nearly a Year
summary:
New home sales continued their recovery in October, returning to levels not seen since the start of 2026. Sales of new single-family homes rose to a seasonally adjusted annual rate of  701,000 , up  14.2%  from September's revised 614,000 and 7.5% above October 2025.    The number of new homes for sale fell to  470,000 , down 1.5% from September and 4.1% from a year earlier. With sales rising and inventory declining, the implied supply dropped to  8.0 months , down from 9.3 months in September and 9.0 months a year ago.  Prices continued to soften. The median sales price slipped to  $391,300 , down 0.3% from September and 3.2% from October 2025. The average sales price fell to  $459,900 , down 2.2% month over month and 12.1% year over year. As a reminder, prices in this data set do not take into factor changes in square footage, neighborhood, etc.

title: Purchase Applications Post Strongest Week Since September
summary:
Mortgage applications rebounded as rates eased over the course of the week, despite a slight increase in the weekly average. The Mortgage Bankers Association (MBA) reported a  6.1% increase  in total application volume for the week ending November 20, 2026.  Purchase applications improved by 10% on a seasonally adjusted basis, and Refinance applications increased just 1%. On an unadjusted basis, purchase activity was up 5% for the week.  Despite the rebound, purchase applications remained  16% below year-ago levels , while refinance activity was down  51% . The refinance share of total applications fell to 40.1% from 41.1%, while adjustable-rate mortgage applications increased to 11.5%, their highest share in more than a year.  MBA's Joel Kan noted that purchase applications reached their strongest weekly pace since September, likely benefiting from rates declining over the course of the week. Freddie Mac's average 30-year fixed rate nevertheless increased to  7.38% , its highest level in five weeks. Kan also pointed to the growing appeal of ARMs, with the average ARM rate at 6.39%, nearly a full percentage point below the 30-year fixed rate.   Mortgage Rate Summary:

title: Home Price Appreciation Remains Positive
summary:
Home prices continued to post modest annual gains in September. The  S&P Cotality Case-Shiller  National Home Price Index rose  2.1%  year over year in September, matching August's gain. The 10-City Composite increased  3.5% , down slightly from 3.6% in August, while the 20-City Composite rose  2.6% , unchanged from the previous month.    Monthly results offered a somewhat more encouraging picture after accounting for seasonal patterns. The National Index  rose  0.2%  on a seasonally adjusted basis. The 10-City Composite followed the same pattern, while the 20-City Composite posted a 0.1% seasonally adjusted gain.   The latest  FHFA  data also showed continued appreciation, with national home prices rising  2.5%  between the third quarters of 2025 and 2026. Prices increased 0.7% from the second quarter, although the seasonally adjusted monthly index was unchanged in September. All nine census divisions posted positive annual appreciation, led by the Middle Atlantic at 4.9%. The Pacific division recorded the weakest gain at 0.5%.   FHFA House Price Index

title: Mortgage Rates Only Modestly Higher
summary: Mortgage rates rose only modestly on Friday despite bond market weakness suggesting a slightly bigger change. The Friday after Thanksgiving is always "interesting" when it comes to the secondary market that underlies mortgage rates. There are far fewer traders present and liquidity is hard to come by.  In today's case, higher stock prices put upward pressure on bond yields and interest rates. There's no way to know if this is simply the incidental byproduct of the thin liquidity and light volume or if it's indicative of supportive undertones in the stock market that might continue next week.

title: Another Mortgage Fraud Case; Equity and Non-Agency Product News; VantageScore and Credit Thoughts
summary: Don’t do the crime if you can’t do the time. A Jacksonville mortgage broker has pleaded guilty to making a false statement five years ago to influence a mortgage lending business after submitting altered bank statements and fabricated employment documents to secure a VA-guaranteed home loan. Desean Antoin Ford, 55, of Jacksonville, faces a maximum penalty of 30 years in federal prison. Turkey (and other lean meats) is a staple in prison… Just ask Lee Farkas of TBW who was released from prison during COVID and never went back. Interestingly, U.S. citizens have steadily been eating less turkey over the past several years. For most of the 1990s and early 2000s, turkey consumption was pretty stable, with the average American consuming 17-18 pounds a year. But by 2015, the average American was down to 16 pounds of turkey per year, and today, consumption has fallen sharply to 13.2 pounds. However, consumption of chicken is up 50 percent over the three-decade period from 1995 (when the typical American consumed 69 pounds of chicken annually) to 2025 (when they consumed 104 pounds). Chicken has managed to beat turkey on price, and as the average size of a U.S. household declined, chickens were better at producing the correct amount of meat for a household than the comparatively larger turkeys.
